findings.reason: as written the node's gate cannot pass however well the restructure works, so a worker either reports a failed gate it could not have satisfied or leaves the section's stated lever for one the plan never measured; the bound has to be re-derived from the 351.44 s base (for example from the 220.67 s the two passes hold, with the residual 130.8 s stated) before dispatch.
findings.text: done-when (2) requires the production row program's cold compile to reach "45 s or less (351.4 s at that base)" while the section's own cited profile gives that base 351.44 s of XLA compile with `variadic-op-splitter` at 160.48 s and `multi_output_fusion` at 60.19 s; even if the restructure removed both passes entirely it would leave 130.8 s, and this profile states the splitter costs `39.9 s per 100,000` post-splitter instructions, so the done-when's companion clause of halving 402,141 to about 201,070 instructions lands near 80 s of splitter time alone and a head arm near 240 s. The bound is the decision `compile-target-shared` value of 45 s (95.1 s − 51.3 s ≈ 44 s, at line 103), carried to a base 3.7 times larger; the sentence "it is not relaxed for the larger base" applies an arithmetic that only held at 95.1 s.
